newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-INTERVIEW-Metal Man eyes mid-yr upturn.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-INTERVIEW-Metal Man eyes mid-yr upturn.

text.p: Metal Manufactures Ltd said on Wednesday it was hopeful that Australia's depressed housing sector would see a recovery by mid-1997 and that this would flow through to the group's second half earnings.
"Hopefully around the mid-year a (housing) market turnaround will be starting to emerge," the company's managing director, Glenn Dudley told Reuters in an interview.
Metal Manufactures is 61.5 percent owned by British cables and construction group BICC Plc.

Metal Manufactures supplies all the optic fibre cable for the cable television roll-out programs being conducted in Australia by Optus Vision and by Vision Stream for the Foxtel joint venture between Telstra Corp and News Corp Ltd.
"The optic fibre program is ongoing for the development of both those carriers networks. Whilst we will see some downturn - we see that gap being filled by export orders," he said.
"We are fairly uncertain about when that (housing upturn) will be. The near perspective, I have to say, is that we have not seen any sign of that upturn in our businesses as yet," he said.
Metal Manufacturers earlier posted a net profit of A$38.5 million for the 1996 calendar year compared to A$46.85 million in 1995 and cut its final dividend to seven cents from 10 cents.
Dudley said the company expected its first half earnings would reflect a continuation of the flat housing market conditions that have existed for the past 12 months.

Dudley said the BICCOR joint venture between its 50 percent owned BICC Cables Asia Pacific and Corning Inc, had been set up specifically to develop optical cable manufacturing facilities in emerging markets in Asia.
"Its very early days. This venture is planned to capture those growing markets (in Asia) - its a three to five year plan," he said.
Metal Manufactures and Corning have a joint venture optical fibre manufacturing operation in Melbourne.
The other half of BICC Cables Asia is owned by BICC Plc.
Dudley said the company's dispute with the Australian Tax Office (ATO) over potential liabilities of A$31.6 million was ongoing and any resolution was in the hands of the ATO.
Metal Manufactures shares last traded at A$3.17 on March 4.
